curation.notes: Dual-trap optical tweezers (LUMICKS C-Trap Edge-450, two instruments) stretch single biotinylated mitotic chromosomes isolated from HeLa Ki-67-mEmerald cells (WT, Ki-67 knockdown, overexpression) in a bead dumbbell; force-extension at 0.02 and 0.2 µm/s plus a step-and-hold broadband microrheology analysis (2.5 MHz force data) fitted with a Burgers model. HILO (pseudo-TIRF) fluorescence imaging acquired simultaneously.

evidence.snippet: High frequency (2.5 MHz) force data over the 2 min dwell period was used in the microrheology analysis.
Trap stiffness was calibrated for every new bead pair in the absence of fluid flow and was 0.5 ± 0.03 pN/nm at each bead.
A pair of streptavidin-coated polystyrene beads (3 μm diameter, Bangs Laboratories) in PA buffer was optically trapped in the first microfluidic channel with the two optical traps.
linearly displacing the second trap position along the x-axis at a fixed rate of 0.02 μm/s to measure linear elasticity and 0.2 μm/s to examine chromosome non-linear stiffening behaviour
The trapped bead pair was then moved across to the channel flowing chromosomes suspended in PA buffer (channel 2) to capture a single biotinylated chromosome first by binding to one bead.

entities.name: Ki-67-mEmerald (chromosome periphery organiser; WT, knockdown, overexpression)

evidence.snippet: Homology-directed repair (HDR) plasmids designed to introduce mEmerald to the C-terminus of MKI67 were synthesised using a pUC18 backbone
